synopsis: Earned-value forecasting is a comparator in the corpus’s assessment of reference class forecasting, whose advantage over it and Monte Carlo depends on a genuinely similar reference class [f9437, f16315, f9606]. Batselier and Vanhoucke’s 2016 empirical test found that advantage across accuracy, stability and timeliness, but only when reference-class similarity was high [f9606]. The glossary reinforces this condition with a 2025 review concluding that reference class forecasting works only when the right reference classes have been constructed [f16315]. These findings therefore do not establish unconditional superiority over earned-value forecasting [f9437, f16315, f9606].

relations.note: Both condition reference class forecasting’s comparative advantage on genuine reference-class similarity.
Identifies the 2016 empirical test and specifies accuracy, stability and timeliness.
The conditional empirical advantage supports the glossary’s requirement for appropriately constructed reference classes.
